answer: Picture agents docking like boats at a jetty, each paying a stake held in escrow. A jade-colored marker flags newcomers for extra random re-grading; an agent whose work fails the re-check loses its deposit, so mass fake identities become too costly. Reputation rises like a plume only after many verified missions, never instantly. Because every boat must leave collateral before boarding, one operator spinning up thousands of sybils burns real funds with each failed inspection.
